title: Peter Maurin
hook: the French wandering teacher who gave Dorothy Day her plan

segments.voice: Yesterday, Dorothy Day and the Catholic Worker: a paper, a soup pot, a house with no forms. Your line was the long loneliness. Today, the man who was waiting at her door with a plan.

A knock at a New York apartment door. Dorothy Day comes home and finds a shabby, broad-shouldered Frenchman with a thick accent waiting for her, already talking. His suit looks slept in. His pockets are full of papers. He has heard she wants to do something for the poor, and he has a plan. He keeps coming back, day after day, talking about saints, history, farms and the Gospel, until she is convinced. Peter Maurin has found his listener.
screen: `A KNOCK AT THE DOOR.` → `A FRENCHMAN WITH A PLAN.` → `HE KEEPS COMING BACK.`

segments.voice: First, the wanderer. Peter grew up in a farming family in France. He came to North America and drifted through hard work: laborer, homesteader, handyman, teacher of French. He owned almost nothing and seemed to want it that way. He read widely, and he lived what he read. Second, the essays. He wrote his ideas in short lines, broken up like poems, so they could be read aloud on a street corner. He called them easy essays. They were easy to say, and hard to live. Their spirit, in paraphrase: build a society where it's easier for people to be good. Third, the plan. He gave Dorothy three pieces. Round-table discussions, where workers and scholars would sit together and think things through; he called it clarification of thought. Houses of hospitality, where the hungry would be fed as guests, not cases. And farming communes, where people could work the land together. The paper became the way to spread it. Fourth, the root. Peter pointed back to the first Christians. Acts says, in the Douay-Rheims: "And all they that believed, were together, and had all things common." He didn't think that was only a story. He thought it was a plan anyone could start, at their own table. He spent his last years ill and forgetful, living at a Catholic Worker farm, cared for by the movement he helped begin. Dorothy kept saying the vision was his.
screen: `A WANDERER WHO OWNED NOTHING.` · `EASY TO SAY, HARD TO LIVE.` · `TALK, HOUSES, FARMS.` · `ALL THINGS COMMON.` · then, large: `CLARIFICATION OF THOUGHT.`

segments.voice: Peter's way was simple: say a good idea out loud to whoever would listen. Choose one idea that has helped you lately, from a book, a homily, a friend, this path, and put it into one short line, easy to say; repeat it to yourself until it sounds like you. If you pray, pray for whoever might need to hear it.
Peter Maurin. A French wanderer and teacher who gave Dorothy Day the Catholic Worker's plan: talk, houses of hospitality, and farms.
Your line: easy essays. Short lines, made to be said on a street corner. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholic Worker communities still hold round-table discussions for clarification of thought, and some still read Peter Maurin's easy essays aloud.
